data.note:
2026-08-19 18:23 - Design guidance (human question, 2026-08-19): the same image runs many times per repo with fresh clones — do NOT let that imply per-task image builds.

Layering:
1. BASE IMAGE, pinned to the tk version (same cadence as the factory bundle, which tk factory deploy already version-pins): git, the harness CLIs, language runtimes. Built and pushed at deploy time, instantiated per run. Starting the Nth container costs no rebuild.
2. REPO DEPENDENCY CACHE — persisted, never baked into the image. Baking node_modules means rebuilding the image on every lockfile change, which is the treadmill this question is trying to avoid. Prefer a named sandbox per project whose filesystem survives sleep/wake (pnpm store, ~/.cache/go-build, ~/.cargo), so a fresh clone lands in a warm container. Snapshot/restore is the alternative.

HARD CONSTRAINT (axiom 1): cache warmth is convenience state. A cold sandbox with an empty cache must always produce a CORRECT run — warmth buys speed, never correctness. Never let a green build depend on a warm worker. Verify the actual Sandbox persistence/snapshot API rather than assuming it; this epic already paid once for assuming a platform behaviour (the PBKDF2 cap).

Related gap, flagged not assigned: .tick/config.md has an Environment section, but it is VERIFICATION only (test, don't ask). There is no place to declare how to WARM a repo (pnpm install --frozen-lockfile in cloud/factory, go mod download). A 'Setup' section — idempotent, cache-populating commands — would give this entrypoint something to run and would help local runs too. 2026-08-19 18:28 - Design correction + constraint (human question, 2026-08-19). My earlier note said the image is 'built and pushed once at tk factory deploy' — too absolute. The real question is where PER-REPO TOOLCHAIN provisioning happens, and it is now a hard constraint rather than a preference:

The epic has just documented 'one factory, many projects — adding a repo is ENROLMENT, not deployment'. If enrolling a repo required building and pushing a container image, that statement is false. So the image design must make adding a repo cost ZERO image work.

Rejected: a per-repo image (enrolment becomes a build, and N images must each stay pinned to the tk version). Also rejected as the primary answer: a fat base image carrying every runtime — cold starts are per-tick in Phase 2, so image size is a recurring cost, and it is always eventually missing a toolchain, at which point every project pays for a rebuild.

Preferred: THIN BASE + PROVISIONED TOOLCHAIN. Base carries git, the harness CLIs and a version manager (mise/asdf-class) — nothing repo-specific, rebuilt only when tk or a harness version changes. The entrypoint provisions the repo's declared toolchain on first run for that project, landing in the project's persistent sandbox so it is warm from run two onward — the same cache mechanism as dependencies. Adding Rust support then becomes a line in one repo's config, not a factory-wide rebuild.

Toolchain declaration source: prefer the ecosystem's own pins (go.mod, package.json, .tool-versions) over inventing a format. .tick/config.md Environment is VERIFICATION only, so it cannot serve here — same gap as the missing Setup section.

Escape hatch: a repo may pin a custom image explicitly, opt-in, for genuinely exotic needs.

Unchanged: axiom 1 — first run cold and slow is fine, every later run warm; a cold sandbox with an empty cache must still produce a CORRECT run.
